name: Cindergrain Patchwork Survivor's Full Kit
description: A head-to-toe layering system assembled over years rather than purchased at once. The base is a long-sleeved thermal compression shirt in faded ash-gray, its original branding long since worn to illegibility, seams reinforced with overlapping strips of orange self-repair tape that have themselves begun to fray at the edges. Over that sits a quilted vest of salvaged insulation panels — mismatched grays and a single panel of rust-brown — stitched together with thick black upholstery thread in visible X-patterns. The outer layer is a hip-length work jacket in washed-out olive canvas, its left sleeve replaced entirely with a sleeve from a different jacket in charcoal wool, and its collar stiffened with a strip of recycled polymer sheeting to deflect acid-rain splash. Both chest pockets are reinforced with riveted leather patches. Cargo pants in dark charcoal synthetic twill hang heavy with accumulated gear — four deep pockets on each thigh sealed with mismatched industrial snaps, the knees double-patched in rubber-backed fabric for crawling on Shelf grating. A worn leather belt carries a utility loop on each hip. Boots are a resoled pair of thick-soled work boots, the uppers cracked and sealed repeatedly with black rubber sealant compound, the toe caps re-wrapped in salvaged steel plate fixed with pop rivets. A knit balaclava in dark gray — hand-stitched where moth damage opened holes — can be pulled up to cover the lower face against acid mist.
functionality: Multi-layer acid-rain resistance via polymer collar and sealant-treated outer shell. Deep cargo pockets for survival gear. Knee reinforcement for crawling through industrial ruins. Balaclava seals against airborne particulate. Boot toe caps provide impact protection. Self-repair tape maintains structural integrity of failing seams.
what_it_says: This person has survived the Shelf long enough to know exactly what kills you and has patched against each threat individually. The mismatched materials aren't carelessness — they're a biography of close calls and salvage runs. No single piece is new. Everything has been repaired at least twice.
manufacturer: Self-assembled from salvage, no single maker
price_range: Φ12–Φ40 (assembled over time from scrap markets)
story_hooks: A Circuit-tier investigator stops the wearer at a checkpoint — the self-repair tape on the jacket matches a chemical signature from a recent industrial break-in, and suddenly a survival kit becomes evidence.

The salvaged steel toe caps on the boots are stamped with a Crucible Corponation serial number from a batch reported stolen three years ago — someone is very interested in finding out where the wearer got them.
In a Shelf food line, another survivor recognizes the charcoal wool sleeve as having been cut from a jacket belonging to someone who disappeared six months ago.

physical_description.visual_profile: A weathered, deliberately asymmetrical survivor's silhouette. The figure reads as a walking archive of salvage and repair — layers of protection stacked without aesthetic concern, only function. The mismatched sleeve colors create visual tension. Everything is oversized enough to move in, tight enough to stay secured. The overall impression is grimy resilience: someone who has crawled through industrial infrastructure and lived to tell it.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately relaxed and utilitarian. Compression base layer hugs torso for heat retention; quilted vest adds bulk without restriction; work jacket hangs loose for layering and quick movement. Cargo pants sit low on hips with room in the thighs for gear loops and tool access. Boots are chunky and heavy. All seams and closures are sized for gloved hands.
physical_description.primary_material: Base: faded synthetic thermal weave (originally branded, now illegible). Vest: salvaged foam insulation panels. Jacket: washed olive canvas with charcoal wool replacement sleeve. Pants: dark charcoal synthetic twill. Belt: worn leather. Boots: cracked leather uppers, thick rubber soles. Reinforcements: orange self-repair tape, black upholstery thread, riveted leather patches, rubber-backed fabric, black rubber sealant, pop rivets, recycled polymer sheeting.
physical_description.texture: Deeply tactile and lived-in. The compression shirt is soft but pilled from wear. Quilted vest has visible stitch lines creating texture grid. Canvas is stiff and worn smooth in high-contact areas. Wool sleeve is slightly fuzzy. Leather is cracked with raised sealant ridges. Orange tape is fraying at edges. Boots are sealed and re-sealed, creating a bumpy, reinforced texture. Balaclava is loose-knit with visible hand-stitching repairs.
physical_description.color_scheme: Muted, industrial palette: faded ash-gray base, orange self-repair tape (worn to pale orange), rust-brown quilted panel, charcoal wool, olive-washed canvas, dark charcoal twill, black thread and sealant, weathered leather browns, dark gray knit. No bright colors. Everything is either washed-out or artificially dulled by wear and chemical exposure.
closures: Thermal shirt: side seams reinforced with overlapping orange tape
Vest: hand-stitched with thick black upholstery thread, no traditional closures
Jacket: canvas snap buttons (some missing, improvised with rope ties on some)
Cargo pants: mismatched industrial snap closures on all thigh pockets
Belt: worn leather with brass buckle
Boots: salvaged laces, pop rivets securing steel toe caps
distinctive_features: Asymmetrical jacket: entire left sleeve replaced with charcoal wool from different source
Polymer sheeting collar reinforcement for acid-rain deflection
Riveted leather chest pocket reinforcements — visible hardware
Double-patched rubber-backed knee panels designed for crawling on industrial grating
Four deep thigh cargo pockets per leg with industrial snaps
Utility loops on belt hips for tool attachment
Boots with salvaged steel plate toe caps fixed with pop rivets
Hand-stitched balaclava with visible moth-damage repairs
Orange repair tape throughout, itself fraying — showing layered repair history
Visible black upholstery thread stitching in X-patterns on vest
All original branding worn to illegibility — no corporate markers
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 (sub-grade/ungoverned). This is salvage assembled over years, not purchased. No corporate manufacture markers, no warranty seals, no new-purchase crispness. Every repair is visible and permanent. The wearer has chosen function over status.
physical_description.cultural_context: This is the uniform of the Shelf-dweller, the scrap-crawler, the infrastructure salvager. Wearing this announces: 'I work in industrial ruins, I am not connected to corpo supply chains, I repair rather than replace, I know how to move through dangerous spaces.' The visible repairs are not aesthetic choices — they are badges of survival. This outfit says the wearer has hands-on knowledge of acid-rain zones, industrial grating, confined spaces, and equipment maintenance.
physical_description.condition_typical: Perpetually broken-in. This is not a outfit that looks 'new' or 'pristine' at any point in its lifecycle. The visible orange tape is already fraying. The sealant on the boots is cracked and will crack again. The balaclava has been repaired by hand and will need repairs again. Wearing this outfit means accepting that it will only get more weathered — the goal is to keep it functional, not fashionable.
